adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: Bobby leads the break-in at the old mansion to free Rogue from Cerebro. As the Sentinels close in, he holds them off so she can escape, and they kill him while she screams his name.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Her ex. Dies so she can escape the Sentinels.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: His ex. He dies freeing her from Cerebro.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): Iceman proposes rescuing Rogue from Cerebro at the former X-Mansion; he and Magneto free her and Iceman is killed by Sentinels covering their escape (Wikipedia); 'screaming Bobby's name as he sacrificed himself' (fandom Rogue page). Kind friend: in this version Bobby is dating Kitty (they kiss), so the couple from X-Men: The Last Stand is over. See owner_calls.

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: With Xavier guiding them, Magneto and Bobby break into the old mansion and free Rogue from Cerebro. After Bobby falls to the Sentinels, Magneto gets her back to the X-Jet.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Once his captive. Freed by him from Cerebro.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Once her kidnapper. Frees her from her prison in Cerebro.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): 'With Xavier's guidance, Iceman and Magneto successfully infiltrate the mansion and rescue Rogue... Rogue and Magneto make it aboard the X-Jet' (fandom plot). Turns the tie from enemy (X-Men, X2) to ally.

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: Xavier agrees to rescue Rogue from Cerebro, guides the break-in from the X-Jet and flies her out. At the temple she takes over holding Logan's mind in the past for his plan.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A former student he rescues from Cerebro.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Her old teacher. Leads her rescue from the old mansion.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): Xavier agrees to help Iceman rescue Rogue; Xavier, Magneto and Iceman succeed; Rogue then keeps Wolverine's mind in 1973 (Wikipedia; fandom Rescue of Rogue lists Professor X as commander).

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: When Kitty weakens, Rogue copies her power and takes over holding Logan's mind in 1973, and in the past he senses the change.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Holds his mind in the past when Kitty can't.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: An old friend whose mind she holds in 1973.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): 'Rogue uses her power to take over for Kitty in regards to keeping Wolverine's mind in 1973... Wolverine is aware of the switch as he appears to feel Rogue's presence' (Wikipedia).

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: Rogue reaches the temple and tells the wounded Kitty that Bobby didn't make it, then copies Kitty's power and takes her place holding Logan's mind in the past.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Takes her place holding Logan's mind in the past.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A wounded X-Man whose power she copies.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): 'Rogue arrives at the remote Chinese monastery... solemnly informs Shadowcat that Iceman didn't make it before copying her powers and taking her place' (fandom plot). New tie.

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: When Kitty is hurt, Bobby tells Xavier that Rogue is held in Cerebro and could take her place. Xavier agrees to the rescue and guides Bobby into the old mansion.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A former student who dies on the rescue he guides.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: His old teacher. Agrees to his plan to save Rogue.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): Iceman 'informs both Xavier and Magneto' that Rogue is imprisoned in Cerebro; 'Xavier agrees to help Iceman rescue Rogue'; 'With Xavier's guidance, Iceman and Magneto... infiltrate the mansion' (fandom plot). New tie; see owner_calls (the two also know each other in earlier films).

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: Magneto and Bobby break into the old mansion together to free Rogue. Bobby stays behind to hold off the Sentinels so Magneto can get her out.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: An X-Man who covers his escape with Rogue.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: An old enemy he breaks into the mansion with.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): 'Iceman and Magneto successfully infiltrate the mansion and rescue Rogue... Iceman is killed while buying enough time for the others to escape' (fandom plot). New tie.

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: At the old mansion, Bobby holds off the Sentinels so Rogue and Magneto can escape, and they kill him.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Robots that kill him at the old mansion.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: An X-Man they kill at the old mansion.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): 'They are soon discovered by the Sentinels, Iceman tries to hold them off but gives his life so that Magneto and Rogue can escape' (fandom Rescue of Rogue; Wikipedia: rescue 'at the cost of Iceman's life'). New tie (also missing for the regular version, where Sentinels kill him at the temple).

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: Rogue is held prisoner in Cerebro at the Sentinel-guarded mansion. Sentinels attack as she escapes, killing Bobby, and another strikes the X-Jet as she boards.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Robots that guard her prison and kill Bobby.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A captive mutant who escapes them.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): Rogue 'is currently imprisoned in Cerebro... the X-Mansion is too heavily guarded'; 'the three of them are attacked by a group of Sentinels'; 'Rogue and Magneto make it aboard the X-Jet, but... they are attacked by another Sentinel' (fandom plot). New tie.

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: When Magneto is badly hurt in the Sentinel attack on the temple, Kitty phases him through to safety inside.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Badly hurt. Pulled to safety by her.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Pulls him to safety inside the temple.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): 'After Magneto is severely injured during the ensuing Sentinel attack, instead of Blink creating a portal... Shadowcat uses her phasing ability to pull him inside' (fandom plot; movie-censorship comparison also lists Kitty pulling Magneto in). New tie.

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: When Xavier lays out his plan to send Logan back to 1973, Bishop argues against it, since some of them may never be born. Xavier and Storm talk him round.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Doubts his plan, then backs it.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Talks him into a plan that may erase him.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): 'Bishop is the first to argue against it... he does not want to sacrifice himself for a future where he and the others may never be born... Xavier and Storm are able to convince them' (fandom plot); movie-censorship lists a 58-second added argument with Bishop, Blink, Storm, Sunspot, Magneto and Xavier speaking ('Some of us may never be born'). New tie.

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: Blink sides with Bishop against Xavier's plan to send Logan back to 1973, until Xavier and Storm win her over.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Doubts his plan, then backs it.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Wins her over to his plan to change the past.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): 'Blink and Sunspot are quick to echo his sentiments, but Xavier and Storm are able to convince them otherwise' (fandom plot); movie-censorship lists Blink speaking in the added argument. New tie.

adds.on_a_card_about_b: Doubts his plan, then backs it.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Wins him over to his plan to change the past.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): Same added argument scene: Blink and Sunspot echo Bishop; Xavier and Storm convince them (fandom plot; movie-censorship lists Sunspot speaking). New tie.

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: Storm helps Xavier talk Bishop round when he argues against sending Logan back to 1973.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Argues against the plan until she talks him round.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Helps talk him into Xavier's plan.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): 'Xavier and Storm are able to convince them otherwise' (fandom plot); Storm speaks in the added argument (movie-censorship). New tie.

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: Storm helps Xavier win Blink over when she sides with Bishop against sending Logan back to 1973.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Doubts the plan until she wins her over.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Helps win her over to Xavier's plan.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): Same added argument scene (fandom plot; movie-censorship). New tie.

adds.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
adds.text: Storm helps Xavier win Sunspot over when he sides with Bishop against sending Logan back to 1973.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Doubts the plan until she wins him over.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Helps win him over to Xavier's plan.
adds.evidence: Rogue Cut (2015, 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment): Same added argument scene (fandom plot; movie-censorship). New tie.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Betty interviews Ned about Peter for the school news, and grills her ex about late-night texts.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Her ex. Grilled by her about late-night texts.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: His ex. Interviews him about Peter.
adds.evidence: More Fun Stuff Version (2022 theatrical re-release, Sony): Betty interviews Peter's teachers and classmates; 'Ned is questioned by Betty, his ex, about late-night texts' (Screen Rant). Tie has no No Way Home stage.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Betty interviews Flash about Peter for the school news, and he claims he gave Spider-Man his name.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A classmate who claims he named Spider-Man.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A classmate who interviews him for the school news.
adds.evidence: More Fun Stuff Version: in Betty's interviews, 'Flash claims he gave Spider-Man his name' (Screen Rant; Wikipedia: 'Brant interviewing Peter, his teachers, and his classmates'). New tie.

adds.title: Deadpool 2
adds.text: Wade turns up in Logan's past and shoots the Weapon XI version of himself in front of him. He tells Logan that one day he will ask him to get back in the saddle, and Logan should say yes.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A clawed mutant he asks for a favor someday.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A mercenary who drops in from the future.
adds.evidence: Super Duper Cut (2018 Blu-ray/DVD, 20th Century Fox): after shooting Weapon XI in front of the X-Men Origins Wolverine, Wade tells him he will one day ask him to get back in the saddle and he should say yes; Logan answers 'Huh?' then 'Oh, right' (Screen Rant). New tie; in the regular version they share the same moment but Wade only quips about fixing the timeline. Note: fox-wolverine's titles in people_all.json do not list Deadpool 2, though he appears there (repurposed X-Men Origins footage) in both versions; see owner_calls.

owner_calls.question: In the Rogue Cut, Bobby dies at the old mansion rescuing Rogue, not at the temple. The fox-iceman|fox-kitty-pryde and fox-wolverine|fox-iceman stages for X-Men: Days of Future Past say he is killed defending the temple. Keep them (true for the theatrical cut), or reword so they hold for both versions?
options: Reword to drop where he dies, e.g. 'Bobby fights the Sentinels to protect Kitty while she holds Logan's mind in the past, and he dies in the war' (Kitty) / '...and he does not survive the war' (Logan)
owner_calls.evidence: Wikipedia: Rogue is rescued 'at the cost of Iceman's life (rather than Iceman being killed by the Sentinels during the final confrontation at the temple)'.

owner_calls.question: The Rogue Cut shows Kitty and Bobby dating (extra dialogue and a kiss before she sends Logan back; Wikipedia: 'revealed to be dating Iceman in this version'). Should fox-iceman|fox-kitty-pryde move from friend to partner at X-Men: Days of Future Past? The Rogue/Bobby add above uses friend for the same reason.
options: Change Kitty/Bobby to partner at DOFP and keep Rogue/Bobby at friend
owner_calls.evidence: movie-censorship comparison: 'Kitty and Iceman have extra dialogue and kiss' (Rogue Cut only).

owner_calls.question: The Rogue Cut adds Raven returning to the mansion, nearly rekindling her romance with Hank after he treats her leg, then destroying Cerebro overnight. Does this change what matters most in the fox-raven-darkholme|fox-beast-young DOFP stage (now the Paris fight)?
options: Replace with: 'Hank tends Raven's wounded leg when she returns to the mansion, and they share a tender night. By morning she has wrecked Cerebro so Charles cannot find her.' (ally)
owner_calls.evidence: Fandom plot: 'Mystique returns to the X-Mansion and shares an intimate moment with Beast after he fixes up her wounded leg. During the night, she sneaks into Cerebro and destroys the computer.'

owner_calls.question: The Rogue Cut's added argument also has Logan and Magneto speaking with Bishop, Blink and Sunspot. Ties proposed only for Xavier and Storm (who win them over). Add Logan and Magneto ties with Bishop, Blink and Sunspot too?
options: Add Logan/Magneto ties with all three
owner_calls.evidence: movie-censorship lists Bishop, Wolverine, Blink, Storm, Sunspot, Magneto and Professor X all speaking in the added 58-second scene; who answers whom is not given.

owner_calls.question: New ties fox-charles-xavier|fox-iceman, fox-magneto|fox-iceman and fox-iceman|fox-sentinels would first appear at DOFP, but Bobby is Xavier's student and fights Magneto in X-Men (2000)/X2/The Last Stand, and Sentinels kill him in the theatrical DOFP too. Should a later pass give those ties earlier stages?
options: Yes, queue for the full pass
owner_calls.evidence: Untied in ties_all.json despite shared films.

owner_calls.question: Daredevil (2003) Director's Cut adds the Dante Jackson murder case: Matt and Foggy defend Jackson, Matt interrogates a dirty cop (McKenzie), and Foggy and Karen Page trace the killing of Urich's informant to Wesley, which helps bring down the Kingpin. None of the sources found say Foggy or Matt face Wesley or Fisk in those scenes, and Jackson, McKenzie and this film's Karen Page are not in the app. Check the disc for a Foggy/Wesley or Foggy/Kingpin exchange, and add those people?
options: Check the disc and add stages if they meet
Add Dante Jackson / Karen Page (2003) as people
owner_calls.evidence: Wikipedia: subplot 'involving a drug addict played by Coolio, who was charged with killing a prostitute informant who was feeding Urich info on the Kingpin'; Marvel fandom: 'Foggy learning Wesley's connection to Lisa Tazio's murder'.

owner_calls.question: The Punisher (2004) Extended Cut is built around Jimmy Weeks, Frank's friend who sold him out to Howard Saint (Kuwait prologue, park and street scenes, Howard pressing Weeks in the casino, Frank making him shoot himself). Weeks is not in the app, so no stages can be added. Add him as a person?
options: Add Jimmy Weeks with ties to Frank (friend then enemy), Howard Saint and the Toro brothers
owner_calls.evidence: movie-censorship comparison of the Extended Cut; Wikipedia: 'most of which revolves around the character Jimmy Weeks'.

owner_calls.question: No Way Home: May rides an elevator with Norman, Otto, Max and Flint, and works with them at Happy's condo in both cuts, but May is untied to Otto, Max and Flint. Raise for the full pass? Also noticed: Peter (sv-peter-parker-raimi) and Rosalie Octavius are untied though they dine together in Spider-Man 2.
owner_calls.evidence: Screen Rant: elevator ride with Peter, May, Electro, Doc Ock, Norman Osborn and Sandman on the way to Happy's apartment.

owner_calls.question: The proposed fox-deadpool|fox-wolverine stage is at Deadpool 2, but fox-wolverine's titles do not include Deadpool 2. He appears there in both versions through reused X-Men Origins: Wolverine footage. Add Deadpool 2 to his titles so the stage shows up, or drop the stage?
options: Add Deadpool 2 to fox-wolverine's titles and keep the stage
owner_calls.evidence: Screen Rant: the post-credits scene reuses Hugh Jackman footage from X-Men Origins: Wolverine; in the Super Duper Cut Wade asks him to say yes one day, and Logan answers 'Huh?' and 'Oh, right'.
